key_insight: Brine imbibition can mobilize trapped hydrogen in heterogeneous sandstone even at very low capillary numbers, but recovery depends strongly on flow rate and pore-scale heterogeneity.
engineering_relevance: Hydrogen storage models and injection/withdrawal strategies must account for pore-scale heterogeneity and transient trapping to predict recoverability and storage efficiency.
method: Fast in-situ synchrotron X-ray micro-CT to visualize hydrogen redistribution during brine imbibition
Systematic variation of brine injection rate to test flow-rate effects
Quantification of trapped and mobilized hydrogen clusters in a heterogeneous sandstone
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct micro-CT observations showing significant mobilization of disconnected hydrogen clusters during imbibition, including at capillary numbers below 10^-6.
watch_item: The findings come from a specific heterogeneous sandstone and pore-scale experiment, so scaling them to field reservoirs will require caution and additional validation.
paper_title: Flow-rate controls on trapped hydrogen redistribution in a heterogeneous sandstone: a synchrotron X-ray micro-CT study
